Title: Simulation and optimization of nutrient uptake and biomass formation using a multi-parameter Monod-type model of tobacco BY-2 cell suspension cultures in a stirred-tank bioreactor

Abstract: Results and discussion: The biomass formation was well predicted by an unstructured segregated mechanistic Monod-type model as long as the nutrient concentrations did not approach zero (we omitted phosphate, which was completely depleted). Model: improved unstructured model with sucrose hydrolysis
Laws:
(2) [balance] Active biomass balance accounts for growth and loss through conversion to dead biomass.
(3) [balance] The cultivation-medium volume changes at a rate equal to the feed rate.
(5) [balance] Sucrose balance in the BY-2 cultivation medium, including feed input and cellular uptake.
(6) [balance] Nitrate balance in the BY-2 cultivation medium, including feed input and cellular uptake.
(7) [balance] Ammonium balance in the BY-2 cultivation medium, including feed input and cellular uptake.
(8) [balance] Phosphate balance in the BY-2 cultivation medium, with uptake independent of active biomass.
(18) [constitutive] Specific growth rate combines ammonium and phosphate growth contributions with saturating and inhibitory responses to glucose or fructose and nitrate.
(19) [balance] Fructose accumulates in the variable-volume medium from sucrose hydrolysis and is depleted by uptake by active cells.
(20) [balance] Glucose accumulates in the variable-volume medium from sucrose hydrolysis and is depleted by uptake by active cells.

States (computed by the ODEs):
- V: Volume of the cultivation medium
- X_{a}: Viable (active) cell dry mass
- S: Sucrose concentration
- N: Nitrate concentration.
- A: Ammonium concentration.
- P: phosphate concentration
- F: fructose
- G: glucose concentration

Inputs (variables no law computes):
- F_{t}: Feed rate
- S_{f}: Sucrose concentration in the feed medium
- N_{f}: Feed-medium nitrate concentration.
- A_{f}: Feed-medium ammonium concentration.
- P_{f}: phosphate concentration in the feed medium

Model-wide assumptions:
- The model assumes an irreversible progression in which active cells (active DM) are converted into dead cells (dead DM).

answer.description: The model describes biomass formation and macronutrient uptake in tobacco BY-2 cell suspension cultures, predicting active biomass, medium nutrients, and sugars. It combines nutrient-dependent Monod-type growth and active-to-dead biomass conversion with sucrose uptake and hydrolysis to glucose and fructose, their uptake, and variable-volume medium balances with feed inputs.
